**Bank of England selects three firms for digital pound lab experiments**

*NOBO, Dun and Bradstreet and Polygon Labs will explore programmable payments and commercial data integration in the BoE's latest digital pound sandbox round.*

The Bank of England has selected three firms for the next phase of its digital pound lab: NOBO, Dun and Bradstreet, and Polygon Labs. Each will explore different aspects of how a retail central bank digital currency could work in practice, from consent-driven wallet transaction data to commercial intelligence integration.

NOBO's involvement centres on combining open finance signals with wallet transaction data, while Dun and Bradstreet brings commercial credit intelligence including its proprietary business datasets. Polygon Labs, a blockchain infrastructure firm, adds a distributed ledger dimension to the experiments. The mix of participants reflects the BoE's interest in testing how a digital pound might interact with both traditional financial data and newer technology stacks.

The selections come as the European Parliament has voted to advance the digital euro to final negotiations. While the UK's digital pound remains at an earlier stage than its eurozone counterpart, the lab programme is the primary mechanism through which the BoE is testing design choices and use cases before any decision on whether to proceed.

*Sources: [BoE Digital Pound Lab Picks NOBO, D&B and Polygon Labs](https://thefintechtimes.com/boe-digital-pound-lab-picks-nobo-db-and-polygon-labs/) — The Fintech Times*

**Mollie launches pay-by-bank in the Netherlands using GoCardless infrastructure**

*The first major product integration since the two companies combined tests whether a merged entity can challenge iDEAL and Wero on cost.*

Mollie has launched a pay-by-bank product in the Netherlands, connecting directly to Dutch consumer bank accounts using open banking technology inherited from its acquisition of GoCardless. Mollie CEO Koen Koppen has positioned the product as a lower-cost alternative to both iDEAL and Wero for Dutch merchants.

The launch is the first significant commercial integration since Mollie completed its 1.1 billion euro acquisition of GoCardless in September. By routing payments through open banking rails rather than card networks or scheme-based systems, Mollie is betting that cost savings will be sufficient to shift merchant behaviour in a market where iDEAL already dominates online checkout. The competitive dynamics are sharpened by the ongoing migration of iDEAL volumes to Wero, which introduces its own pricing and governance structure.

Mollie's move illustrates how acquirers that have absorbed open banking infrastructure are beginning to deploy it commercially across Europe. Pay-by-bank's ability to compete with entrenched local payment methods on conversion rates and consumer experience, not just price, remains the central question.

*Sources: [Mollie Strengthens Pay by Bank to Power the Next Generation of European Payments](https://glenbrook.com/payments_news/mollie-strengthens-pay-by-bank-to-power-the-next-generation-of-european-payments/) — Glenbrook | [How Mollie's Pay by Bank Powers Next Gen European Payments](https://fintechmagazine.com/news/how-mollies-pay-by-bank-powers-next-gen-european-payments) — FinTech Magazine*

**GOV.UK One Login to add open banking as identity verification method**

*Citizens will be able to verify their identity via bank account data on the UK government's central digital identity platform, extending open banking into public services.*

The UK Government Digital Service is planning to add open banking as a verification method within GOV.UK One Login, the government's central digital identity platform. Citizens will be able to confirm their identity by sharing verified bank account data, alongside existing methods such as passport and driving licence checks. The rollout is expected in 2027.

The integration follows the government's earlier adoption of Adyen for open banking payments on GOV.UK Pay, and broadens the role of open banking from a payment channel to an identity layer within public services. Using bank-held data for identity verification leverages the fact that banks have already completed KYC checks on their customers, effectively repurposing compliance data as a public good.

Embedding open banking into the state's own identity infrastructure creates a reference use case for the UK's open finance trajectory, one that could accelerate adoption in adjacent sectors such as healthcare, local government and benefits administration.

*Sources: [Monaco startup advances heartbeat biometric authentication](https://www.biometricupdate.com/202610/monaco-startup-advances-heartbeat-biometric-authentication) — Biometricupdate*

**Experian launches consumer reporting agency for cashflow-based underwriting**

*A dedicated credit reporting entity built around open banking transaction data intensifies competition with fintechs such as Plaid in the lending decisioning market.*

Experian has launched a new consumer reporting agency specifically designed for cashflow-based underwriting, using open banking transaction data as its primary input. The entity is structured as a standalone reporting agency, giving lenders a regulated framework for using real-time bank transaction data in credit decisions alongside traditional credit bureau scores.

The move positions Experian as a direct competitor to open banking providers such as Plaid, which has been expanding beyond account connectivity into income verification and lending decisioning across the UK and Europe. By wrapping open banking data in a formal credit reporting structure, Experian is offering lenders something the pure-play open banking firms have struggled to provide: regulatory familiarity and integration with existing credit infrastructure.

Cashflow-based underwriting is moving from experimental to institutional. The Financial Conduct Authority's recent signals on using open banking data for mortgage affordability checks and rent payment history further reinforce the direction of travel. Experian's entry as an established credit bureau validates the model while raising competitive pressure on the fintech firms that pioneered it.

*Sources: [Experian Unveils New Consumer Reporting Agency for Cashflow Underwriting](https://finovate.com/experian-unveils-new-consumer-reporting-agency-for-cashflow-underwriting/) — Finovate*
